newsitem.title: FRANCE: French airports seek DHL Strasbourg project.
newsitem.headline: French airports seek DHL Strasbourg project.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express said it has received telephone calls today from a "significant number" of French provincial airports offering their facilities as a Rhine Valley air cargo hub in place of its Strasbourg-Entzheim project.

Steven Lewis, DHL Aviation's business development manager, told Reuters from Brussels that the company is also seeking a meeting with the French Transport Ministry, in the next month, to discuss new locations in eastern France.
This follows the Strasbourg Chamber of Commerce asking DHL to withdraw its application.
"While Strasbourg remains our first choice, we do not expect to make any new proposals for at least several months. In the meantime, we will be considering other sites,"

Lewis said that on September 16, DHL proposed a six-month trial to Strasbourg' urban community council. This included measures to re-examine aircraft approaches to the airport, the re-routing of flights away from built-up areas as well as other noise reductions measures, but the trial was turned down, he added.

"The climate is just not right at present to re-submit proposals. Moreover, we need to find out just what would be acceptable to the local people and how much scope this will give us to modify our plans."
DHL said it is currently achieving annual growth of 20 percent in turnover and 30 percent in tonnage from its European activities.
Main shareholders in DHL are Deutsche Lufthansa AG and Japan Air Lines Co Ltd who each hold a 25 percent stake. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +44 171 542 5017
